stem:
Bharat slides a steel box across a smooth glass table and then across a rough wooden table.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Friction between the box and the rough wood is greater because of more irregularities, so the box stops sooner.
Friction between the box and the wood pulls the box forward and speeds it up.
Friction acts on the box even when the box is not touching any table.
Friction slows a sliding box only on wooden tables, never on glass.

teacher.key_rationale: Friction is an opposing interaction between surfaces in contact and is greater on rough wood. Saying friction speeds the box up reverses opposition. Acting with no contact drops the contact condition. Limiting friction to wood alone over-narrows the rule.

mx_swap.reason: Sibling-term swap for friction invents a neighbouring label not in the stem; kept relationship_reversal, condition_omission, and scope_error on the contact-opposition hinge.
